bibl.title: GEPIA2: an enhanced web server for large-scale expression profiling and interactive analysis

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: gene- and isoform-level expression across TCGA tumour and GTEx normal samples
span.quote: Featuring 198 619 isoforms and 84 cancer subtypes, GEPIA2 has extended gene expression quantification from the gene level to the transcript level, and supports analysis of a specific cancer subtype, and comparison between subtypes.

span.label: how to make expression, survival and signature analysis of TCGA/GTEx available at isoform and cancer-subtype resolution
span.quote: Featuring 198 619 isoforms and 84 cancer subtypes, GEPIA2 has extended gene expression quantification from the gene level to the transcript level, and supports analysis of a specific cancer subtype, and comparison between subtypes.

span.label: a web server extending expression quantification from the gene to the transcript level and to 84 cancer subtypes, with user-uploaded data comparison and a python API
span.quote: Featuring 198 619 isoforms and 84 cancer subtypes, GEPIA2 has extended gene expression quantification from the gene level to the transcript level, and supports analysis of a specific cancer subtype, and comparison between subtypes.

span.label: method
span.quote: GEPIA2 performs survival analyses based on gene or isoform expression levels. Given a list of custom cancer types, GEPIA2 would provide a heat map to show the survival analysis result based on multiple cancer types (Figure 2A).

span.label: prognostic associations that appear only at cancer-subtype resolution
span.quote: It is thus desirable to perform prognostic analysis at a higher resolution. Based on the outputs of GEPIA2, we found that MAPK6 showed no association with breast cancer survival while it exhibited significant association with unfavorable prognostic outcome in Lumina A subtype

span.label: interactive analysis over UCSC Xena recomputed TCGA and GTEx RNA-seq, served from a relational database
span.term: interactive analysis over UCSC Xena recomputed TCGA and GTEx RNA-seq, served from a relational database
span.quote: In GEPIA2, we utilized the UCSC Xena recomputed data of TCGA and GTEx for 198,619 coding and a series of other non-coding transcripts, and developed new computational functionalities to explore such events.

span.label: alternative splicing shifts which isoform of a gene predominates, and the shift can be specific to a cancer type
span.quote: Users can view the protein translation of each isoform in different cancer types and find the cancer specific isoform or isoform ‘switch’ event in a certain cancer type.

span.label: a user's uploaded matrix and the server-side target set are quantile-normalised against each other before any differential test, so the comparison is between normalised distributions rather than raw counts
span.quote: After the Quantile-normalization or other two additional normalization strategies (inspired by GenomeSpace) based on the uploaded dataset and the target dataset on the server, GEPIA2 performs the differential expression analysis and return result in boxplot.

span.label: the Cancer-subtype Classifier is described as predicting accurately, and the article reports no accuracy, no held-out split and no confusion matrix anywhere
span.quote: With this function, users can accurately predict the cancer type or cancer-subtype of their uploaded samples based on the gene expression. The classifier is trained by TCGA expression data.

span.label: the two classifier modes trade sensitivity against coverage, and the paper states the trade-off without quantifying either side
span.quote: We provide two modes to work with the classifier by choosing the actual cancer type first and predict for its corresponding subtypes or directly predict with the range of all cancer subtypes. The former way provides a more sensitive result, and the latter will be more useful for the identification of the cancer with unknown origin.

span.label: prognostic gene lists in the prior literature were derived at cancer-type level, so a subtype-specific effect is invisible in them
span.quote: These prognostic genes were identified based on a general cancer type rather than cancer subtype. However, different cancer subtypes in a cancer type can be distinct. For instance, triple-negative breast cancer has a ∼15% lower five-year survival rate compared to other breast cancer subtypes.

span.label: gene signature quantification, taken from single-cell sequencing practice into bulk TCGA/GTEx analysis
span.quote: However, the existing data cannot present the expression distribution of a certain immune-cell cluster across cancer types. In this case, researchers can use GEPIA2 to easily obtain the immune-cell cluster signature profile in a pan-cancer manner. For example, one can readily find that Th1-like signature in stomach tumors is significantly higher than that in adjacent normal tissues (Figure 2C).

span.label: any accuracy, precision, recall or held-out validation figure for the Cancer-subtype Classifier
span.note: eliminates: a classifier that is confidently wrong - no accuracy, precision, recall or held-out figure is given for a tool the sentence says predicts cancer subtype `accurately` · outcome: absent-declared-unreported
span.quote: With this function, users can accurately predict the cancer type or cancer-subtype of their uploaded samples based on the gene expression. The classifier is trained by TCGA expression data.

span.label: the same MAPK6 survival test run at whole-breast-cancer level alongside the Lumina A subtype level
span.note: eliminates: a survival signal that exists only in one subtype being reported as a property of the cancer type · outcome: held
span.quote: (D) The overall survival analyses based on the cancer type and cancer subtype showed the significant prognostic impact of MAPK6 in Lumina A breast cancer subtype (left, P = 0.022) but not the whole breast cancer (right, P = 0.15).

span.quote: This function analyzes the prevalence of a gene signature in TCGA and GTEx samples. The mean value of the log2(TPM + 1) is used as the signature score.

span.label: hazard ratios
span.quote: The heat map shows the hazard ratios in logarithmic scale (log10) for different genes. The red and blue blocks denote higher and lower risks, respectively.

span.label: 'Stacked' = pool the selected subtypes, then compare the pool with normal samples
span.quote: For the Box Plots feature, once users select the custom subtypes, they can select ‘Stacked’, ‘Separated’ or ‘Comparing Across Subtypes’ for different purposes. ‘Stacked’ indicates the approach to combine all the samples from selected subtypes prior to differential expression analysis with normal samples. ‘Separated’ means the method to perform differential expression analysis separately with normal samples. ‘Comparing Across Subtypes’ selection performs the differential expression analysis among the selected subtypes.

span.label: 'Separated' = compare each selected subtype with normal samples on its own
span.quote: For the Box Plots feature, once users select the custom subtypes, they can select ‘Stacked’, ‘Separated’ or ‘Comparing Across Subtypes’ for different purposes. ‘Stacked’ indicates the approach to combine all the samples from selected subtypes prior to differential expression analysis with normal samples. ‘Separated’ means the method to perform differential expression analysis separately with normal samples. ‘Comparing Across Subtypes’ selection performs the differential expression analysis among the selected subtypes.

span.label: 'Comparing Across Subtypes' = compare the selected subtypes with each other, not with normal

span.quote: GEPIA2 python API provides users with access to GEPIA2’s analyses from a programming environment. Designed to perform multiple requests for our service, it boosts the efficiency of users by allowing batch process and streamlining results retrieval. The API is implemented in python language and we provide a tutorial for users to utilize the API. The python package provides access to 5 functionalities: boxplot, similar, correlation, survival and survival map.
